Russian Anti-War Politician Ends Political Campaign After Pressure from Kremlin — Russian opposition politician Boris Nadezhdin has withdrawn from the September State Duma election after authorities blocked his campaign, labeled him a “foreign agent,” fined him over alleged extremist symbols, and restricted his movements. The assailant reportedly struck the teenager and forced him and a companion off the vehicle.

Foreign Engineers for Ukraine: A Strategy for Victory? — Ukraine’s defense industry is producing military technology at an unprecedented pace, but a shortage of engineers and technical specialists is emerging as a major challenge. US forces also targeted elements of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) responsible for a July 17 attack on US personnel in Jordan.

Kyiv Protests Grow: Calls to Reinstate Fedorov and Oust Ukraine’s Commander-in-Chief — Protests in Kyiv on Saturday, July 18, have expanded from calls to reinstate former Minister of Defense Mykhailo Fedorov to demands for the dismissal of Ukraine’s Commander-in-Chief, General Oleksandr Syrskyi. Protesters accuse Syrsky of obstructing military reforms and hindering the advancement of younger officers – allegations that gained momentum following Fedorov’s public criticism.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened full-scale offensive operations if US strikes continue. US Central Command confirmed targeting Iranian logistics and naval assets.

China Declines to Supply Equipment for Russian Northern Sea Route Fleet — China has declined to supply propulsion and steering systems for Russia’s large-tonnage ice-class vessels due to international sanctions, hindering Moscow’s efforts to develop the Northern Sea Route. Russian shipyards lack the capacity and domestic equipment to build the required Arc7 ice-class tankers. Local authorities in the Tambov region reported the deaths of seven Wildberries employees.
